RL agents learn representations that are more similar to those of humans than previously assumed, and that the learned representations are strongly affected by hyperparameters of the training process.

the visual representations and saliencies of RL agents trained on Atari games are similar to human saliencies, and that these similarities and differences explain the agents' performance on the tasks.

(1) The visual representations learned by deep RL algorithms are similar to the visual representations of human experts, but they do not capture all of the same information, and (2) RL agents can learn to perform tasks more efficiently by focusing on more task-relevant features.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following three main objectives: 1) to investigate whether RL algorithms are able to learn human-like representations of the task environment; 2) to investigate how the learned representations of the task affect the performance of the RL agent; and 3) to investigate how different hyperparameters of the RL algorithms affect the learned representations.

the saliency of human and machine attention is correlated, and this correlation is affected by the hyperparameters of the RL algorithm.
